answer: Topological cut verifications resist Sybil attacks by auditing peer clusters along network bottlenecks. A peer auditing pool uses stake slashing to punish fake identities: a verifier observing cross-boundary flows flags fraudulent collusions. Like a falcon hunting prey across a cedar grove, auditors spot cloaked sable nodes, forcing attackers into superlinear staking costs O(N^2) to fabricate persistent graph cuts.
